questions.question: Yamini Krishnamurthy was recognised as the 'Asthana Narthaki' of which style of dance?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yamini Krishnamurthy** is one of the most renowned dancers in India, recognized for her mastery in **Bharatanatyam** and **Kuchipudi**.
 
• She was honored as the '**Asthana Narthaki**' (court dancer) of the **Thanjavur style of Bharatanatyam** and also excelled in **Kuchipudi**, a classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Bharatanatyam**, originating from Tamil Nadu, is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India and is known for its **expressive gestures, intricate footwork, and spiritual themes**.
 
• **Kuchipudi**, originating from Andhra Pradesh, combines **graceful movements with dramatic storytelling**, often performed with music and dialogue.
 
• Yamini Krishnamurthy’s contributions to these dance forms have earned her **national and international recognition**, including prestigious awards such as the **Padma Shri** and **Padma Bhushan**.
 
• She has been an inspiration to countless dancers, and her performances reflect the **rich heritage and spirituality** of Indian classical dance.
 
• Her dedication to promoting these dance forms led her to establish dance academies and mentor aspiring dancers, ensuring the **preservation and growth of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Odissi and Kathak**__

 __
 
• **Odissi** is a classical dance form from **Odisha**, characterized by its **fluid movements and sculpturesque poses**. It is deeply rooted in temple traditions and often depicts **stories of Lord Jagannath.**
 
• **Kathak**, originating from **North India**, is known for its **intricate footwork, spins, and storytelling**. It has influences from both **Hindu** and **Mughal cultures**.
 
• While Yamini Krishnamurthy is associated with Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi, her contributions do not extend to these dance forms.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali and Manipuri**__
 __
 
• **Kathakali**, from **Kerala**, is a classical dance-drama known for its **elaborate makeup, costumes, and facial expressions**. It often portrays stories from the **Mahabharata and Ramayana.**
 
• **Manipuri**, originating from **Manipur**, is a devotional dance form that focuses on themes of **Vaishnavism** and stories of **Lord Krishna**.
 
• Yamini Krishnamurthy has not been associated with these dance forms, as her expertise lies in Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniattam and Sattriya**__
 
 
• **Mohiniattam** is a classical dance form from **Kerala**, characterized by its **graceful and feminine movements**. It is performed mainly by women and depicts **stories of love and devotion.**
 
• **Sattriya**, from **Assam**, is a dance form associated with **Vaishnava monasteries** and is known for its **spiritual themes and storytelling.**
 
• Yamini Krishnamurthy has not trained in or performed these dance forms.

questions.question: In 1887, whose work did Heinrich Rudolf Hertz apply to conduct a series of experiments from which he generated radio waves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Clerk Maxwell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Clerk Maxwell** was a Scottish physicist who formulated a set of equations that describe the behavior of **electric and magnetic fields**, known as Maxwell's equations.
 
• Maxwell’s equations predicted the existence of **electromagnetic waves**, which could travel through space at the speed of light.
 
• **Heinrich Rudolf Hertz** applied Maxwell’s theoretical work in 1887 to conduct experiments that demonstrated the existence of **radio waves**.
 
• Hertz’s experiments involved the generation of electromagnetic waves, confirming Maxwell’s prediction and laying the foundation for the development of **wireless communication technologies**.
 
• Maxwell’s contributions are considered a cornerstone of modern physics, as his equations unified the fields of **electricity, magnetism, and light.**
 
• The confirmation of Maxwell's theory by Hertz eventually led to the invention of the **radio, television, and radar systems**.
 
• Maxwell’s work is a significant milestone in the development of the field of **electromagnetic theory**, influencing various scientific and technological advancements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Christiaan Huygens**__

 __
 
• **Christiaan Huygens** was a Dutch mathematician, physicist, and astronomer known for his work on the **wave theory of light**.
 
• He proposed the **Huygens-Fresnel principle**, which describes how wavefronts propagate.
 
• Huygens invented the **pendulum clock**, significantly improving timekeeping accuracy.
 
• While his work on waves was influential, it primarily focused on **light**, not the electromagnetic waves described by Maxwell.
 
 
 
• **Christian Doppler**__
 __
 
• **Christian Doppler** was an Austrian physicist best known for the **Doppler effect**, which describes the change in frequency or wavelength of a wave in relation to an observer moving relative to the source of the wave.
 
• The Doppler effect has applications in **astronomy, weather radar, and medical imaging** (e.g., Doppler ultrasound).
 
• His work is unrelated to the generation or propagation of **radio waves**.
 
 
 
• **Thomas Young**__
 
 
• **Thomas Young** was an English polymath known for his contributions to the **double-slit experiment**, which demonstrated the wave nature of light.
 
• He also made significant contributions to the fields of **vision, elasticity, and linguistics.**
 
• Young’s work focused on **optics and mechanics**, not electromagnetic waves or radio wave generation.

questions.question: Which of the following plants is a Pteridophyte which is usually found in moist, shady places or gardens and on hills where the temperatures are low?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ferns**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ferns** are classified as **Pteridophytes**, which are vascular plants that reproduce via spores rather than seeds.
 
• They thrive in **moist and shady environments**, making them common in gardens, forests, and areas with high humidity.
 
• These plants are often found on **hills** or in regions with **low temperatures**, which provide the ideal conditions for their growth.
 
• Ferns possess a well-developed vascular system, including **roots, stems, and leaves**, which allows them to transport water and nutrients efficiently.
 
• They exhibit a unique alternation of generations, involving a **sporophyte** (diploid) and a **gametophyte** (haploid) phase.
 
• Ferns are considered primitive plants but play a significant role in **maintaining ecological balance** and are often used in landscaping for their aesthetic appeal.
 
• Examples of commonly known ferns include **Adiantum (Maidenhair Fern)**, **Pteris**, and **Dryopteris**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sphagnum**__

 __
 
• **Sphagnum** is commonly known as peat moss and is classified as a **Bryophyte**.
 
• It grows in **wetlands**, such as bogs and marshes, and is known for its ability to retain water.
 
• Sphagnum has a significant role in the formation of peat, which is used as **fuel** and in agriculture as a soil conditioner.
 
 
 
• **Riccia**__
 __
 
• **Riccia** is a genus of **liverworts** that belongs to the Bryophyte group.
 
• It is typically found in damp and moist places and is characterized by its **thalloid structure**.
 
• Unlike Pteridophytes, Riccia lacks a vascular system and reproduces through spores.
 
 
 
• **Porphyra**__
 
 
• **Porphyra** is a type of **red algae** and is not a vascular plant.
 
• It is commonly found in **marine environments**, especially in intertidal zones.
 
• Porphyra is widely cultivated for its use as **nori** in sushi and other food products.

questions.question: Mayurbhanj Chhau is a tribal dance form of _____.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mayurbhanj Chhau** is one of the three distinct forms of Chhau dance in India, originating from the **Mayurbhanj district of Odisha.**
 
• It is a **tribal dance form** that combines elements of martial arts, folk traditions, and classical dance.
 
• Unlike other Chhau forms such as Purulia Chhau or Seraikela Chhau, Mayurbhanj Chhau does not use **masks** in performances.
 
• The dance is known for its **vigorous movements** and intricate footwork, depicting themes from **epic stories** such as the Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
• Mayurbhanj Chhau employs **martial postures** and movements, showcasing the strength and agility of the performers.
 
• The costumes are elaborate, and the dance is accompanied by traditional music played using instruments such as **drums (Dhol), cymbals, and reed instruments.**
 
• It has been recognized as an **Intangible Cultural Heritage** by UNESCO, highlighting its cultural and historical significance.
 
• Mayurbhanj Chhau is a form of **ritualistic storytelling** that reflects the rich cultural heritage of Odisha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Tripura**__

 __
 
• **Tripura** is known for its rich cultural heritage and tribal traditions, but it does not have any major association with the Chhau dance form.
 
• The state is famous for its indigenous dances such as **Hojagiri** (performed by the Reang tribe) and **Garia dance**, which are linked to its tribal communities.
 
• Tripura's dances often reflect themes of nature, agriculture, and folklore.
 
 
 
• ** Bihar**__
 __
 
• **Bihar** is culturally significant but is not historically known for Chhau dance.
 
• The state is renowned for its folk dances such as **Bidesia** and **Jat-Jatin**, which reflect the rural life and traditions of the region.
 
• Bihar’s cultural practices are largely influenced by its association with the ancient kingdoms of Magadha and Maurya.
 
 
 
• ** Assam**__
 
 
• **Assam** is known for its famous dance forms such as **Bihu**, which celebrates the harvest festival.
 
• Other notable dances include **Sattriya**, a classical dance form rooted in Vaishnavite traditions, and **Bagurumba**, performed by the Bodo tribe.
 
• While Assam has a rich repertoire of dance forms, it is not associated with the Chhau dance tradition.

questions.question: How many members were there in the Constituent Assembly on 31st December 1947?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**299**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **31st December 1947**, the **Constituent Assembly of India** had a total of **299 members.**
 
• The **Constituent Assembly** was established to draft the **Constitution of India**, which came into effect on **26th January 1950.**
 
• The assembly originally had **389 members**, but after the partition of India in 1947, the number reduced to **299 members.**
 
• Out of the 299 members, **229 represented British India**, and **70 represented the princely states.**
 
• The assembly was chaired by **Dr. Rajendra Prasad**, who later became the first **President of India.**
 
• The work of the Constituent Assembly was divided into several committees, such as the **Drafting Committee**, chaired by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, which was responsible for preparing the draft of the Constitution.
 
• The assembly met for a total of **165 days** spread over **2 years, 11 months, and 18 days** to deliberate on the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• The Constituent Assembly played a vital role in shaping the legal and institutional framework of India, incorporating values of **justice, equality, liberty, and fraternity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Historical Contributions of the Assembly:**__

 
 
• The assembly drafted and adopted the **Indian Constitution**, which is one of the largest written constitutions in the world.
 
• It incorporated important principles like **Fundamental Rights**, **Directive Principles of State Policy**, and provisions for a **federal structure.**
 
• Prominent leaders such as **Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Patel, Maulana Azad, and B.R. Ambedkar** contributed significantly to the debates and discussions.

questions.question: Out of the following events, which event is NOT a part of Competitive Yogasana Sports?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Rhythmic Yogasana (Single)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rhythmic Yogasana (Single)** is not included as part of **Competitive Yogasana Sports**.
 
• Competitive Yogasana Sports focus on showcasing **strength, flexibility, balance, and artistic expression** through specific formats such as **Artistic Yogasana (Single & Pair)** and **Traditional Yogasana**.
 
• **Rhythmic Yogasana** is primarily associated with a synchronized flow of movements performed to music, emphasizing aesthetics rather than competitive scoring.
 
• It does not align with the standardized rules and scoring system defined for **Competitive Yogasana Sports**, which prioritize measurable physical performance.
 
• The formats of **Competitive Yogasana Sports** include specific poses, choreography, and techniques that adhere to globally recognized standards of competition.
 
• Exclusion of **Rhythmic Yogasana** ensures clarity in competition categories and avoids overlapping with other performance arts.
 
• The focus of Competitive Yogasana Sports is on poses and sequences that demonstrate the essence of traditional and artistic yoga practices rather than rhythm-based performances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Traditional Yogasana**__

 __
 
• **Traditional Yogasana** is a core component of Competitive Yogasana Sports, focusing on poses that are **rooted in classical yoga practices**.
 
• It emphasizes the **discipline of holding static postures** for a defined duration, showcasing stability and alignment.
 
• Examples of poses include **Padmasana, Chakrasana, and Sarvangasana**, which are integral to traditional yoga.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Yogasana (Single)**__
 __
 
• **Artistic Yogasana (Single)** involves a solo performance of yoga postures combined with **flowing movements and choreography**.
 
• It focuses on **grace, expression, and creativity** while maintaining the essence of yoga poses.
 
• This format is scored based on **presentation, difficulty, and execution**.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Yogasana (Pair)**__
 
 
• **Artistic Yogasana (Pair)** is performed in pairs, emphasizing **synchronization and coordination** between two participants.
 
• It includes choreography and poses that require **teamwork and balance**.
 
• This format highlights the harmony and interaction between participants, making it unique in Competitive Yogasana Sports.

questions.question: As per SRS Bulletin 2020, what was the birth rate in India?

• The **birth rate** is defined as the number of live births per 1000 people in a year.
 
• The SRS Bulletin is one of the most reliable sources of demographic data in India, published by the **Registrar General of India (RGI).**
 
• The data helps in understanding trends in **population growth**, planning for healthcare, and allocation of resources.
 
• The birth rate is influenced by several factors such as **education levels, healthcare access, economic conditions, and social norms**.
 
• India's declining birth rate over the years is indicative of improving **family planning measures** and increased awareness about **reproductive health.**
 
• The birth rate varies across states in India, with states like **Bihar** having higher rates compared to states like **Kerala**, which often report lower rates.
 
• Tracking the birth rate is crucial for achieving sustainable development goals (SDGs), especially those related to **healthcare, education, and poverty alleviation.**

questions.question: What was the impact of the global oil crisis of 1973 on the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-1979)?

options.text: It had no significant impact on the plan.
Led to a reduction in agricultural focus

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Caused economic disruptions and re-prioritisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **global oil crisis of 1973** was triggered by the **Arab Oil Embargo**, resulting in a sharp increase in crude oil prices worldwide.
 
• The oil crisis had a significant impact on India’s economy, especially during the planning of the **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–1979)**.
 
• This economic shock disrupted the government’s planning process and forced the **re-prioritisation of developmental goals**.
 
• Higher oil prices increased the **import bill**, leading to a rise in inflation and a deterioration in the balance of payments.
 
• The plan had to address the issue of **energy security** and focus on reducing dependence on oil imports by promoting domestic energy production.
 
• The crisis underscored the importance of **resource mobilisation** and necessitated adjustments to the original plan, including curtailing ambitious expenditure.
 
• The government shifted focus to sectors like **agriculture and rural development**, which were deemed critical for ensuring food security and employment in the face of economic instability.
 
• The plan also emphasised **poverty alleviation programs** and social sector investments to mitigate the adverse effects of the crisis on vulnerable sections of the population.

questions.question: In which of the following Five-Year Plans was the minimum needs programme introduced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fifth Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Minimum Needs Programme (MNP)** was introduced during India’s **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–1979)**.
 
• The programme aimed to provide a basic standard of living to the people by ensuring access to essential services such as **education, health care, drinking water, sanitation, nutrition, and housing.**
 
• It was designed to reduce **poverty and inequality**, focusing on rural development and the upliftment of underprivileged sections of society.
 
• The **Fifth Five-Year Plan** shifted its focus from growth-centric policies to welfare-centric policies due to widespread poverty and unemployment.
 
• The plan was influenced by the idea of **“Garibi Hatao” (Remove Poverty)**, popularized by then Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• The introduction of the Minimum Needs Programme was in line with the government's goal to ensure **social justice** and eliminate disparities between urban and rural areas.
 
• Under MNP, priority was given to areas like **primary education**, rural health care, rural roads, and rural electrification.
 
• This programme laid the foundation for subsequent policies targeting **inclusive growth** and the welfare of marginalized communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Third Five-Year Plan**__

 __
 
• The **Third Five-Year Plan (1961–1966)** focused on **agriculture and industry** and aimed to make India self-sufficient in food production.
 
• This plan emphasized growth through a balanced approach between **industry and agriculture.**
 
• However, its goals were largely disrupted due to the **Indo-China war in 1962** and economic challenges faced during that period.

questions.question: The celebrations for which of the following festivals are held for ten days in the month of Chingam (August/September) as per the local traditions in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Onam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Onam** is a major harvest festival celebrated in the Indian state of **Kerala**.
 
• The festival is observed during the **month of Chingam** (August–September), which is the first month of the Malayalam calendar.
 
• Onam lasts for **ten days**, with each day having its own significance and rituals.
 
• The highlight of the festival is the celebration of the return of the legendary **King Mahabali**, whose reign is believed to have been a golden era of prosperity and equality.
 
• During Onam, houses are decorated with **Pookalam** (floral rangoli), traditional feasts called **Onasadya**, and cultural activities such as **boat races, folk dances, and music.**
 
• One of the main attractions of Onam is the **Vallam Kali**, or the famous snake boat races, which are held in various parts of Kerala.
 
• Onam is celebrated by people of all religions in Kerala, reflecting the state's **cultural diversity and unity.**
 
• The festival is recognized as **Kerala's state festival** and attracts tourism due to its vibrant traditions and activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Pongal**__

 __
 
• **Pongal** is a harvest festival celebrated primarily in the Indian state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It is observed during the month of **January** and marks the beginning of the Tamil month **Thai**.
 
• The festival lasts for **four days** and is dedicated to the **Sun God** and agriculture.
 
• Key activities during Pongal include cooking the traditional dish **Pongal**, decorating houses, and performing rituals to honor cattle.
 
 
 
• **Bihu**__
 __
 
• **Bihu** is the major festival of **Assam** and is celebrated in three forms: **Bohag Bihu** (April), **Magh Bihu** (January), and **Kati Bihu** (October).
 
• **Bohag Bihu**, the most prominent, marks the Assamese New Year and the onset of spring.
 
• The festival is characterized by **traditional dances, music, feasts, and cultural performances.**
 
• Bihu celebrates the **harvest season** and strengthens social bonds among communities.
 
 
 
• **Makar Sankranti**__
 
 
• **Makar Sankranti** is a Hindu festival celebrated across India in the month of **January**.
 
• It marks the transition of the Sun into the zodiac sign **Capricorn (Makara)**.
 
• The festival signifies the end of the winter solstice and the beginning of longer days.
 
• Key activities include **kite flying, bonfires, feasts, and offering prayers to the Sun God.**
 
• This festival is celebrated under different names across India, such as **Pongal** in Tamil Nadu, **Lohri** in Punjab, and **Uttarayana** in Gujarat.

• The union territory is divided into two separate districts: **Daman** and **Diu**, located on the western coast of India.
 
• **Daman** is situated near Gujarat, while **Diu** is an island close to the southern coast of Gujarat.
 
• Daman and Diu were former Portuguese colonies and became part of India in **1961**.

• The city is known for its **green spaces** like the **Rock Garden** and **Sukhna Lake**.
 
 
 
• **Dadra and Nagar Haveli**__
 
 
• **Dadra and Nagar Haveli** is a union territory located in western India, bordering Gujarat and Maharashtra.

• It is known for its **lush greenery, tribal heritage, and natural beauty**.
